reason: Ask Roadman magic-link auth gate (commit b91e4658) requires an ask_session JWT cookie or a riderProfileId in the POST body. The QA script (scripts/qa-ask-roadman.ts) currently sends neither, so /api/ask returns 401 auth_required for every request.

error.message: Enter your email on /ask to start a session.

probe.query: My FTP has been stuck at 250W for two seasons. I do four-by-five intervals every Wednesday and can't move the needle. What am I missing?

scorecard.note: All metrics null because no cases executed against /api/ask — auth gate blocks unauthenticated POSTs.

migration_0047_ask_auth.evidence: 401 response surfaces the well-formed auth_required error path defined in src/app/api/ask/route.ts:67-74. If the ask_auth_subscribers / ask_auth_tokens tables were missing, the magic-link flow would 500 on token mint; the fact that the gate is up and returning a clean 401 means the schema is live.

whatIsNeededToRun.summary: The QA script needs a valid ask_session cookie attached to every fetch, OR the script needs to be extended to mint one server-side.

options.name: Complete magic-link flow once and capture cookie
steps: Open the magic link from the resulting email
GET https://roadmancycling.com/api/ask/auth/verify?token=... — response sets the ask_session cookie

Copy the cookie value (7-day TTL) and pass it to the QA script via a new --cookie flag (the script does not yet support this — it'd be a ~10-line patch to scripts/qa-ask-roadman.ts adding the Cookie header to askOnce())

options.name: Mint a JWT directly with the server secret
steps: Read ASK_SESSION_SECRET (or METHOD_SESSION_SECRET / RIDER_SESSION_SECRET fallback) from Vercel env
Import signAskSessionToken from src/lib/ask-auth/auth.ts at the top of qa-ask-roadman.ts
Sign a token for any email at script start, send it as Cookie: ask_session=<jwt> on every /api/ask POST
Caveat: depends on which secret prod is using — verify in Vercel before running

options.name: Pass a riderProfileId in the body
steps: /api/ask bypasses the auth gate when the POST body includes a valid riderProfileId (a paying rider's profile UUID)
Extend BodySchema submission in askOnce() to attach a known profile id
Caveat: this exercises the paid-tier rate limit path, not the email-gated path, so the corpus + rate-limit signal differs slightly

whatIsNeededToRun.recommendation: Option 1 (capture cookie via the real magic-link flow). It is the closest to what an actual /ask user experiences and needs no env-var access. The script patch is small: add --cookie=<value> and pass it through to fetch.
